title: Efficient Linearity of ASASA
summary: Efficient linearity was estimated for a decorrelated two-round Feistel scheme; estimating it for ASASA and comparing the resulting distribution with a random permutation remain open.

formal_statement.body: For the $\mathrm{ASASA}$ construction—an $\mathrm{SAS}$ structure wrapped with $A$ layers—estimate its efficient-linearity parameter and characterize the resulting random variable. Efficient linearity has been estimated for a two-round Feistel scheme surrounded by Vaudenay's decorrelation module, but the corresponding analysis for the $A$-wrapped $\mathrm{SAS}$ structure is more difficult. Determine whether the resulting distribution follows, or is distinguishable from, the distribution expected for a random permutation.

scope.domain: Linear cryptanalysis of the ASASA block-cipher construction, an SAS structure wrapped with A layers.
parameters: Efficient-linearity parameter: the linear-cryptanalytic quantity to estimate for ASASA
scope.unresolved_remainder: Estimate efficient linearity for the A-wrapped SAS structure, characterize the resulting random variable, and determine whether its distribution matches or is distinguishable from that expected for a random permutation.

citations.label: Cryptographic Schemes Based on the ASASA Structure: Black-Box, White-Box, and Public-Key (Extended Abstract)

progress.summary: The source contrasts the unresolved ASASA analysis with an efficient-linearity estimate for a two-round Feistel scheme surrounded by Vaudenay’s decorrelation module. It presents comparison with random-permutation behavior as a separate challenging problem.
